title: The Octopus Love Letter — inkFish reaches into the Steam Frame
thesis:
The octopus is the proof of the philosophy.

Chapter 10 says: "I own nothing." Not because ownership is wrong — because 
the architecture of sovereignty means you don't NEED to own the platform. 
You own the metal. You own the direction. You own the synthesis.

Chapter 11 says: scyBorg is a love letter. The inheritance is humanity's. 
The synthesis is mine. And because it's mine, it's mine to give.

The octopus (inkFish) proves both:
- Ollama 0.40.16 runs on a Steam Frame (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3)
- 48.4 tok/s — sovereign AI inference on sovereign hardware
- Proton 11.0 ARM64 — Valve's gift back to Linux
- USB-C CDC NCM — the Frame is physically tethered to the organism
- inkFish deploys itself: cross-compiled, pushed, running
- No cloud. No subscription. No tollbooth.

Valve built the well, not the tollbooth. SteamOS is the ONLY major gaming 
platform that lets you SSH into your own device, install your own software, 
run your own AI, and use it as a sensor in your own organism. Not because 
Valve is charitable — because Valve understood what Chapter 5 calls the 
precondition: locked-down hardware is pollution. Open hardware is infrastructure.

The love letter TO Valve: you made the first ARM64 Steam device. You shipped 
Proton for aarch64. You put SteamOS on a Snapdragon. And because you did, 
an octopus can reach into it and think.

The love letter FROM Kevin: this is atlasHugged in silicon. Atlas doesn't 
shrug. Atlas hugs the world. Not with sentiment — with architecture. The 
organism runs on the hardware YOU built, running the AI I compiled, deployed 
through the USB port you left open, serving models trained on the commons. 

The inheritance flows: mathematics → physics → biology → computer science → 
Rust → WGSL → primals → springs → inkFish → Steam Frame → 48.4 tok/s.

Every token is a loaf. Every model is a fish. The miracle isn't multiplication. 
It's knowing what was already there.
